title: What Would Jesus Look Like Here?
headline: The Goal Isn’t a Better You. It’s Christ in You.
headline_sub: What Would Jesus Look Like Here?
tagline: The goal is not merely to make a better decision. The goal is to become increasingly recognizable as someone who belongs to Jesus.
seo_title: Becoming Like Jesus, Not Just Better (Romans 8:29) | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Christianity isn't a system for producing Me 2.0. A devotional for men on Romans 8:29 and Galatians 4:19: change requires a destination, and it is Christ.
verse_text: For those God foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son….

scriptures.text: For those God foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son….

items: What thought needs to be captured?
What should replace the old response?
But eventually every one of those questions must lead somewhere.
Christianity is not ultimately a system for producing improved versions of ourselves.
Scripture gives a more specific destination:
conformed to the image of His Son.

blocks.text: The ultimate question becomes: “What would Jesus look like here?”

items: A person can become extraordinarily disciplined, and extraordinarily prideful.
Knowledgeable about Scripture, and increasingly unlike Jesus.
Spiritual formation cannot simply mean “I am changing.”

blocks.text: “If my behavior improves, I must be becoming like Jesus.”

items: But external behavior can change while the heart remains governed by something else.
Someone stops people-pleasing because he has become arrogant.
The opposite of sin isn’t always Christlikeness.
Sometimes following Jesus requires surrendering the version of yourself you were trying so hard to build.
Christlikeness is not niceness. It is a life increasingly ordered under the Father.
Your failure does not remove the opportunity to resemble Jesus.
